newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila undecided on entry of Nobel Prize laureate.
newsitem.headline: Manila undecided on entry of Nobel Prize laureate.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos said on Thursday he had not decided whether East Timorese resistance leader and Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta could enter the Philippines during an international summit in November.
"We will cross that bridge when we come to it," Ramos told a lunch meeting with Manila-based foreign correspondents.

Ramos-Horta, co-winner of this year's Nobel peace prize with East Timor's Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo, has accepted an invitation by private Filipino groups to speak at an international meeting of non-governmental organisations in Manila on November 21-24.
The meeting is being held in parallel with the annual summit of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum to be held at nearby Subic freeport on November 25.
"We will discuss the effects of APEC's trade liberalisation policies on the agricultural sector, the environment and other sectors," said Omi Royandoyan, coordinator of the NGO meeting.
"We are against APEC as a formal trading block because smaller economies are bound to be dominated by bigger economies."

Intelligence sources earlier said Manila was determined to block the entry of East Timorese dissidents to avoid any incidents that might disrupt the APEC summit which Indonesian President Suharto will attend.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move never recognised by the United Nations.
Ramos-Horta fled East Timor before the invasion and has since served as the resistance movement's international spokesman.
The Ramos administration barred Ramos-Horta and other East Timorese dissidents from entering the country in 1994 during an international human rights conference on East Timor.
Royandoyan said organisers of the NGO meet had approached Philippine officials on allowing Ramos-Horta to attend the meeting and were told the chances of his being allowed in were "50-50."
